title: OKR calibration jam: cross-team compact + townline micro-plan (v0.1)
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures the outputs from the OKR calibration jam (Nov 12–18) and translates them into a compact townline micro-plan for the upcoming 6-week window. Goal is to reduce cross-team ambiguity, identify 3 highest-impact escalations, and produce a deployable all-hands agenda that signals tradeoffs clearly to ICs and managers.

Summary of decisions:
- Narrowed company-level objective to: "Deliver consistent 99th%-tile inference latency within target budget across hosted and dedicated SKUs."
- Agreed primary success metrics: p99 latency (ms), effective cost-per-token ($/k token), and % of requests served by cache/batching layer.
- Two guarded KRs (experiment-first): (1) Reduce p99 × 10% on standard chat workload by end of 6 weeks; (2) Improve cache hit rate by 12 pp on high-reuse prefixes; (3) Produce a draft rollback & SLA fallback runbook for Dedicated by week 4.

Owners & quick commitments (week-by-week):
- Week 0 (this doc -> exec signoff): Product + Eng to finalize KR thresholds (Priya Nair).
- Week 1–2: Serving-runtime sprint focusing on kernel-selection telemetry and a p99 hunt (Luca Martinez, Eng-serving-runtime).
- Week 2–3: App-level batching/caching experiments with single-customer canaries (Solutions-eng + Dedicated).
- Week 3–4: Console rollouts: new latency dashboards + routing policy toggle for canary users (Console team, Daniel Green).
- Week 4–6: Harden rollback flows and run SLA failure drills with SRE (Ayesha Khan, SRE).

All-hands & communication plan:
- Pre-all-hands (week 3): Ship a short two-slide primer to staff summarizing the OKR, tradeoffs, and where we need help (owners list above).
- All-hands demo (week 5): 12-minute slate: 3-minute problem setup, 5-minute demo of a canary improvement, 4-minute Q&A. Follow with 1:1 rooms for team leads.
- Follow-up comms: Weekly status notes in #company-okrs and a retrospective doc after week 6.

Risk register (top items):
1) Canaries mask broader variance — Mitigation: schedule multi-region smoke tests and escalate to Dedicated pool early.
2) Observability gaps (missing kernel-level timing) — Mitigation: lightweight telemetry spec in week 1; prioritize in release pipeline.
3) Customer SLA exposure during canary — Mitigation: automated fallback to lower-cost variant + explicit communication to pilot customers.

Open questions to resolve before exec review:
- Exact p99 baseline windows and query sets (Bench team to confirm by Nov 14).
- Risk tolerance bands for early rollouts (Legal + Customer Success input).
- Which dedicated customer(s) are eligible for the week-2 canary (Solutions + Sales narrow list).

Immediate asks from execs: 1) Signoff on the three KRs above; 2) Approve two pilot customers for early canary testing; 3) Endorse the proposed all-hands slot and messaging brief.

Appendix: quick links and notes to self:
- Slack threads: #eng-p99-hunt, #prod-ops-canary, #company-okrs
- Primary artifacts to attach after signoff: telemetry spec, canary runbook, dashboard mockups, pilot customer consent template.
- Next sync: Nov 19, 10:00 PT, 45m deep-dive with leads (calendar invite pending).

Notes on tone: keep language blunt and operational in comms; signal tradeoffs rather than promising engineering miracles. This is a compact, high-focus 6-week window — avoid scope creep.
